question: A triangle has two angles measuring 65° and 45°. What is the measure of the third angle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Angle Sum Property: Total internal angle of a triangle = 180°.

Third angle = 180° − (Sum of known angles)

Third angle = 180° − (65° + 45°) = 180° − 110° = 70°.

**∴ The correct answer is 70°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First angle (∠A) = 65°

Second angle (∠B) = 45°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of angles in a triangle = ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f3eebe293ea4b6d4f857c7651760cb6e62f2be0e730293855ca303c9993f8f0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the third angle be x.

⇒ 65° + 45° + x = 180°

⇒ 110° + x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° − 110°

⇒ x = 70°

**∴ The correct answer is 70°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Types of Triangles by Angles

Acute: All angles 90°.

Exterior Angle Property

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of its two interior opposite angles.

Polygon Angle Sum Formula

The sum of interior angles of any polygon with n sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.
